rulings: R23 (Drew, 2026-09-11): 2022 Topps Chrome #221 Bobby Witt Jr.'s image/photo variation is the SONIC tier -- a distinct card line, address hiq:baseball:2022:topps-chrome:221:image-variation-sonic:no-auto, source cardpedia-drew-ruling-2026-09-11 (PRs #2047/#2049/#2051). Card_catalog confirms this row stands (checklist-backed) and confirms NO SP or SSP variation row was ever minted for #221 -- Beckett's 20-card SP list and 5-card SSP list do not include card 221; Sonic is the card's only variation tier.

Ruling 24 (tierless-variation-unique, #2047 follow-up): a title or field that states an image/photo variation but names NO tier resolves to Sonic for this card specifically, because Sonic is the only variation tier #221 has -- a tier-blind claim is not an ambiguity when only one tier exists to claim. A title that DOES name a different tier word (SP, SSP) is not silent, and is PARKED rather than guessed onto Sonic: the checklist attests no SP/SSP row for this card number, so a title claiming one names a card that does not exist in this product's checklist.

One card, one row, one pool: the census below covers BOTH sold_comps identity fields (cardId partition and hobbyiqCardId) and both address families -- the hiq-slug-partitioned rows (tca-ebay, ebay-user-purchase) and the vendor-id-partitioned CardHedge rows the exact-pool reader ORs in by hobbyiqCardId today. Every entry here RELOCATES (never REPOINTs) so the Sonic cardId partition itself holds the row -- the engine's partition-scoped exact-pool read must find these without depending on the OR fallback.
